counting: Count distinct written lexical forms per sound category. Repetition in multiple contexts, extra senses, inflections used merely as filler, and extra voices do not substitute for lexical depth.
contextDepth: A viable core context should contain at least four different words on each side with compatible target position and pronunciation conditions. Keep thin secondary contexts visible as gaps.
claimLimit: Four and five are product starting thresholds set by the owner, not an optimum established by an experiment.
lexicalSelection: Prefer common, ordinary target-language vocabulary and transparent senses. Avoid recent English-looking loans, proper names, acronyms, unusual archaic words and nonwords as convenient fillers. Do not define target-language membership by remote etymology: historically integrated native-use vocabulary is eligible.
sourcePolicy: Dictionary evidence can establish a headword and sense without certifying our IPA. Distinguish direct entry retrieval, indexed excerpts, and unverified candidates. A study of a contrast does not turn editorial words into study stimuli.

currentExclusions.reason: Owner rejects this recent English borrowing for the core French bank.
Proper name used as a convenient sound example; use ordinary vocabulary.

englishVarieties.en-US-ga: General American reference; specify merger assumptions within relevant contrasts.
englishVarieties.en-GB-ssbe: Standard Southern British reference; not a representation of all UK accents.

audioBoundary: No new speech is generated. Lexical approval, phonetic review and every word-by-voice audio audit remain separate stages.
pronunciationDiversity: Count distinct authored broad IPA forms separately from spellings. Homophones do not supply a new auditory example; the core context needs at least four words and four intended pronunciations per side. X must not share the intended pronunciation of either reference. This is text-level screening, not validated audio.
